description.narrative:
The vision of CCI is: Citizens in BiH understand and participate in developing democratic processes and civil society.
The mission of CCI is: To enable Bosnia and Herzegovina's citizens to achieve their interests and increase influence in the decision-making process.
The strategy of CCI focuses on five different areas:
1) Good governance and citizen participation: Established transparent, responsible, depoliticized, and efficient public administration that responds to citizens' needs and engages citizens in decision-making.
2) Countering corruption and misuse of public resources: BiH society establishes a zero-tolerance rate for all forms of corruption and misuse of public resources.
3) The rule of law and election processes: The improved rule of law in BiH and restored citizens' confidence in the electoral process.
4) EU integrations: State institutions, with the active involvement of civil society, have taken essential steps and reforms in areas important for the accession to the European Union.
5) Sustainable civil society: Improved perspectives for the sustainability of civil society organizations in BiH.
CCI detailed the actions it takes in each of the strategic areas.

Detta är fortsättningen på det strategiska partnerskapet som ges genom kärnfinansiering. CCI:s strategi har fem prioriteringar vilket är följande: (1) god förvaltning och medborgardeltagande; (2) motverka korruption och missbruk av offentliga resurser; (3) rättsstaten och valprocesser; (4) EU-integration samt; (5) hållbart civilt samhälle. Det bedöms att kärnstödet till CCI är i linje med strategin för Sveriges reformsamarbete med västra Balkan och Turkiet 2021–2027. Kärnstödet kommer huvudsakligen omfatta områdena mänskliga rättigheter, demokrati, rättsstatsprincipen och jämställdhet och kommer innefatta följande mål: förbättrad demokratisk samhällsstyrning och ökad respekt för mänskliga rättigheter och rättsstatsprincipen, förbättrade villkor för ansvarsutkrävande, ökad transparens och minskad korruption. Kärnstödet bidrar även till FN:s mål för hållbar utveckling, särskilt SDG 16. Bidraget har även ett starkt samband till vad som krävs för att inleda förhandlingar om anslutning till EU. I sitt yttrande om Bosnien och Hercegovinas ansökan om EU-medlemskap, fastställde Europeiska kommissionen 14 nyckelprioriteringar för att inleda anslutningsförhandlingar. Denna insats kan framför allt relateras till prioritering 1, 7, 11 och 14.

This is the continuation of the strategic partnership through core funding support. CCI´s strategy has five strategic priorities: Strategic area 1: Good governance and citizen participation, Strategic area 2: Countering corruption and misuse of public resources, Strategic area 3: The Rule of Law and Election Processes, Strategic area 4: EU integrations, Strategic area 5: Sustainable Civil Society. The contribution to CCI in the form of core support is assessed as aligned with the Strategy for Sweden's reform cooperation with the Western Balkans and Turkey for 2021–2027. The main contribution of this core support is expected to be in the result area Human rights, democracy, the rule of law, and gender equality, with the following objectives: Better democratic governance and greater respect for human rights and the rule of law, and Improved conditions for accountability, increased transparency, and reduced corruption. This core support also contributes to the UN Sustainable Development Goals, specifically SDG 16. Finally, this contribution is strongly related to the EU accession negotiations. To open negotiations, BiH must implement 14 key priorities set out in the European Commission's opinion. This contribution is especially related to the priorities 1, 7, 11, and 14.

description.narrative:
The reports cover the period from October 2024 to December 2025. This period was one of the most challenging for civil society organizations in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was characterized by increased political pressure, a shrinking civic space, and the closure of USAID the largest supporter of the civil society sector in the country. Together, these factors created a significant financial and strategic gap. During the first six months of 2025, CCI was forced to lay off staff, reduce salaries, and significantly scale back its activities. In this context, Sidas additional support provided in June proved essential for the organizations continued functioning. Given these circumstances, it was not expected that CCI would be able to deliver substantial results in 2025. Nevertheless, the organization exceeded expectations and achieved solid results, contributing not only to the Strengthened democratic development, with increased respect for human rights and freedoms and the rule of law, and gender equality area but also to Faster green transition, energy efficiency and enhanced adaptation to climate change and Enhanced capacity to prevent, manage and resolve conflicts, including increased resilience to hybrid threats.
CCIs operations demonstrate that sustained support to citizens and civil society produces tangible and measurable results. The most significant changes are driven by citizens themselves, who moved beyond passive roles and now are increasingly engaged in addressing local issues, proposing solutions, and demanding the government be effective and efficient. By using grassroots initiatives, structured advocacy, and evidence-based policy work, local actions are transformed into concrete political and institutional changes. This change is particularly evident in the following areas: 1) Good governance and citizen participation: More than 60 CSOs were mobilized to facilitate citizen engagement, contributing to key policy and institutional reforms such as the Mental Health Promotion Program 2025-2027 in Republika Srpska, introducing postpartum depression screening allowance of birth companions throughout labor in public maternity wards in the Federation of BiH through the advocacy campaign We Will Not Die in Silence implemented in cooperation with multiple organizations, amendments to the FBiH Criminal Code to recognize femicide as a distinct criminal offense were finally introduced, also to improve organization of appointments, CCI supported citizen's initiative and implemented a series of activities to introduce electronic waiting lists in four institutions covering over 400,000 patients. Additional initiatives addressed the needs of youth, persons with disabilities, and inclusive community centers. 2) Countering corruption and misuse of public resources: Sixteen initiatives by informal groups targeted concession allocation and waste management leading to bans on illegal construction waste disposal and site rehabilitation formal designation of water protection zones annulment and revocation of environmental permits (limestone facility and two small hydropower plants) multiple arrests related to corruption and illegal coal exploitation and the launch of official investigations into high level irregularities in water concession allocations. These results represent a landmark advancement in the protection of natural resources. 3) Rule of law and election processes: The Coalition Pod lupom lost more than 80% of their budget due to the US cut. However, after the municipal elections in 2025 the number of reports by the Coalition increased five times, while the total number of reports to the Central Election Commission (CEC) increased more than seven times compared to 2022, and as a result, more than BAM 400,000 in fines were issued. Also, Coalition's activities have contributed to electoral reform, especially the introduction of new electoral technologies. This outcome also reflects an unexpected change in the behavior of state authorities, as the CEC demonstrated increasing responsiveness and stronger commitment to safeguarding the integrity of the electoral process using sanctions. CCI and its Pod Lupom Coalition contributed to the CEC revising its sanctions policy and acting in a more transparent and timely manner. The third significant change relates to improved relations between civil society and institutions. The Pod Lupom Coalition has strengthened its role as a credible expert in elections, acting not only as an observer of irregularities but also as a partner providing evidence-based recommendations and reform solutions. The fourth change concerns the strengthened capacity of civil society organizations. Coalition members now advocate more effectively, communicate better with the public, independently run campaigns, and conduct long term election monitoring.
Another notable change is the strengthened link between civil society organizations and their influence on policy making processes. It is mostly visible under the relevant strategic areas: 4) EU integration: Civil society has increasingly moved beyond a traditional advocacy role and positioned itself as a credible and constructive actor in complex reform efforts. Thanks to strengthened analytical, policy development, and advocacy capacities, CSOs in the EU integration process of BiH now play a more proactive role. This was most visible through the development of four comprehensive EU acquis road maps, with an additional road map currently under preparation. 5) Sustainable civil society: CCI supported more than 140 CSOs across the country. Through training, those organizations and 250 participants enhanced their capacities in strategic planning, project management, and communication. As a result, several organizations successfully secured funding, developed strategic plans, and improved their visibility and positioning within the sector.
